decisions.executionNote: Approach the two front supports with both arms in their own workspaces; gradually pitch wrists while preserving elbow-up continuity.
Align each wrist with its support's visible yaw and descend toward a side pinch; depth estimate remains uncertain.
Refine the pinch from wrist images, then close both grippers without assuming retention.
Lift both visibly pinched supports clear, then straighten their yaw and begin moving toward symmetric lower support positions.
Both supports remain visible in the grasps. Move to symmetric base positions and begin a controlled descent.
Set the two base supports down slowly and open both grippers, allowing the final few millimeters to settle without pressing.
Withdraw open grippers upward from the supports, then turn outward toward a two-handed grip on the long board.
The base supports appear upright and symmetric. Align open grippers outside the long board's ends before descending.
Descend symmetrically to the long board's ends and close both grippers for a level two-handed lift.
Lift the long board vertically and level with both grippers closed, checking retention before moving above the supports.
Carry the retained board level over the two upright supports and begin lowering while keeping both ends synchronized.
Lower the board the remaining distance, release it across the supports, and withdraw outward and upward to inspect stability.
The released lower board appears stable on both supports. Clear it and approach the remaining white supports with yaw matched to their visible orientations.
Use the wrist views to refine transverse alignment and yaw while descending above the two remaining supports; keep grippers open.
Correct the visible wrist-image offsets before closing: left inward and slightly back, right inward, with a final slow descent.
The right open finger disturbed the lower board. Retract slightly, pinch the remaining supports, and lift clear so the board can settle; inspect before stacking.
Both new supports are retained, but the lower board is displaced. Move the supports outward to safe staging locations so the lower board can be repaired first.
Set the two held supports safely on the table outside the lower board, then withdraw open grippers to prepare its realignment.
Raise clear of the staged supports and approach the displaced board from above, turning the grippers to match its diagonal ends.
Keep the left arm clear while bringing the right gripper down along the displaced board's aligned end for a controlled single-end grasp.
Close on the aligned right end and lift the board clear of the supports; keep the other arm retracted and inspect retention.
The board was not retained. Reopen and approach its right end more deeply and slightly lower, correcting alignment from the current RGB.
Close at the deeper right-end contact without further downward pressure, then make a small vertical retention test.
The board remained on the support rather than lifting. Reopen and lower the right gripper further, matching the board's new shallower diagonal.
Close the right gripper at the corrected board-end height, then lift vertically to verify retention before attempting realignment.
The right end is now retained but the long board tilts. Bring the left arm above the far end for two-handed support, while raising the right end only slightly.
Keep the right end supported and approach the left end from above with an open gripper, using small continuous increments.
Center the left pinch across the board width, close it, and gently raise the lower end while the right hand holds position.
The left pinch missed, so retract it clear. Keep the retained right end closed and gently counter the board's tilt and diagonal yaw before lowering.
The retained board still slopes down at the left. Raise it clear and apply further slow pitch correction, keeping the left arm withdrawn.
The long board pivots under a single-end grasp. Bring it forward away from the supports and lower toward the table to reset a level two-handed pickup.
With the board now nearly level, bring the left gripper to the visible left end at the same height as the right grasp for synchronized support.
Close the left-end pinch and test a small synchronized lift, keeping both grippers closed and inspecting whether the board follows both hands.
The left hand closed above the sagging end. Reopen, lower to that end's actual height, and move slightly inward across its visible width before closing.
Both ends now appear enclosed. Raise the lower left end toward the right while lifting the board clear of the displaced support.
Lift the two-handed board clear of all supports and move toward an unobstructed staging area behind them, so the shifted base support can be restored.
Carry the level board behind the supports, lowering only after clearing their tops. This temporary placement will free both arms for base repair.
Set the long board on the clear rear table and release both ends, avoiding further contact with the scattered supports.
Withdraw clear of the staged board and turn toward the supports. The displaced front-left base support needs repositioning before rebuilding.
Replan from the interrupted pose using half-size translation and rotation increments, retracting from the rear staging board.
Move the left wrist toward the displaced front support, turning to a forward pinch; keep the right arm clear while the board remains staged.
Approach the front support from behind its visible wrist-image position, keeping the pinch open until alignment and height are confirmed.
Center the left pinch on the displaced support, close, and lift it clear before returning it to the lower-layer position.
Return the retained support to its original base location. Raise and orient the empty right wrist above the work before approaching the staged board.
Set and release the repaired base support, then withdraw upward. Move the right open gripper high above the staged board's end.
Replan after the continuity guard: lower the right wrist while advancing in smaller increments, and bring the left wrist upward toward the other staged-board end.
Center both open grippers on the staged board's ends using the wrist offsets, descending to the known table-level pinch height.
Close both end pinches and lift the staged board level, checking that both ends follow before moving above the restored base.
Carry both retained ends together toward the restored supports, with extra vertical clearance and a small leftward centering correction.
Center the board above both supports and lower gently, then release it to settle flat without pressing the tilted edge into the supports.
Withdraw both fully open grippers outward and upward so the board can settle freely on the two restored supports.
The board is resting on its narrow edge. Bring closed grippers to its front, staying above it, for a small symmetric tipping correction rather than stacking on the edge.
The previous command executed nothing. Replan from the unchanged pose with smaller translation and yaw increments to stay within joint continuity limits.
Finish aligning both closed fingertips toward the board's front face, with clearance above the supports and without crossing arms.
Approach the raised front edge in small synchronized increments, aiming to settle the tilted board flat rather than displace its supports.
Clear the board's raised edge from above, then gently lower the closed fingertips onto it to encourage a flat resting orientation.
The board is now resting on its long edge behind the supports. Contact its upper edge gently from the front to lay it flat on the clear rear table.
The board is visibly flat again. Clear its upper surface and move outward to symmetric end grasps, opening both grippers and turning gradually.
Align the open jaws with the flat board's short ends, remaining above contact height until its width is centered in both wrist views.
Correct both wrist-image offsets toward the board's full width while lowering to table-level grip height; keep the jaws open to avoid edge-only capture.
Close around the full, centered board width and lift both ends equally, checking that the board remains flat rather than rolling in the jaws.
The full board width is retained and appears flat. Move both hands identically, lifting clear before carrying it back over the base supports.
Lower the flat board evenly onto the two upright supports and open both jaws without moving the wrists during release.
Withdraw open jaws well outside the released lower board before turning toward the staged supports, avoiding the contact that previously displaced it.
The lower board remains stable. Align forward-facing open grippers above the two staged supports without bringing fingers back near the board.
Refine the small lateral offsets, descend onto the staged supports, and close both pinches while remaining well outside the lower board.
Lift both supports vertically clear of the lower board, keeping closed pinches, then straighten their yaw and begin the inward transfer.
Both supports remain retained and upright. Transfer them above symmetric middle-layer positions, maintaining clearance over the stable lower board.
Lower the two upright middle supports onto the lower board at symmetric positions, then release with no downward pressure.
Withdraw vertically from both released supports, then move back and outward before turning toward a two-handed middle-board pickup.
The supports remain upright on the lower board. Align both open end grasps above the middle board while staying clear of the tower.
Descend symmetrically to the middle board's ends and start closing across its full width, keeping the completed lower pieces untouched.
